result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the visual noise and list the same alternatives. B goes further: it points out that 16px padding with equal or smaller gaps blurs the cards together, gives an ordered spacing hierarchy with concrete numbers and a 2:1 heading ratio, and says more precisely when a card is justified (things the user can open, select, drag, compare or act on). A offers a broader set of alternatives, including typography, accent bars and shadows, but its examples are less concrete. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the noise and flattened hierarchy and list similar alternatives. A is more precise: it gives a spacing ratio with concrete values, explains the padding-versus-gap problem, and states clearly when a card is justified, which takes in the open/select/drag/compare test and the advice against stacking or nesting surfaces. B covers more techniques, but some, like shadows and accent bars, drift from the question, and its fixes are a little less concrete.
